docs.title: 🎯 What you'll build
docs.text:
This workshop shows you how AI agents work across UiPath Test Cloud for you, and where a tester still makes the call.

  • 🤖 Autopilot works inside the product. In Studio it creates requirements, test cases, and test sets. In Test Manager it evaluates requirements, generates test cases, and runs a test case autonomously.
  • 💻 A coding agent like Codex or Claude Code works from your terminal. With the uip CLI and the UiPath skills, it automates test cases in your Studio project and runs test sets.
  • 🏦 You start from a real design document for the UiBank demo app.

docs.title: 🔑 Key concepts
docs.text:
💻 Coding agent

An AI assistant (e.g., Claude Code) that builds and runs UiPath components from your instructions, using the uip CLI and UiPath skills.

⌨️ uip CLI

The command-line interface coding agents use to talk to the UiPath platform, including Test Manager (uip tm) and Studio projects (uip rpa).

🧩 UiPath skills

Curated instruction packs that teach a coding agent how to work with UiPath correctly. This workshop uses uipath-test, uipath-rpa, and uipath-platform.

📋 Test Manager

The Test Cloud hub for requirements, test cases, test sets, executions, and results.

🤖 Autopilot for Testers

UiPath's built-in testing agents in Studio and Test Manager. They generate and evaluate requirements, generate test cases and test sets, run test cases autonomously, and explain test results.

🪄 Autopilot for Developers

Autopilot in Studio Desktop for building and fixing automations: it generates and fixes expressions from the workflow's context.

docs.title: 🧭 Agentic Testing: Hands-On Session
docs.text: Take the UiBank design document to requirements, test cases, automations, test sets, and executions in UiPath Test Cloud, with Autopilot for Testers, Autopilot for Developers, and a coding agent.

docs.title: 👋 Overview
docs.text:
A QA team at a bank gets a new application description every sprint. Someone turns it into requirements. Someone types the test cases into Test Manager by hand. Someone else rebuilds each one in Studio, capturing every field and button. A fourth person groups them into test sets, runs them, and copies the results into a status email. That's four handoffs and hours of clicking, and the document, the requirements, the test cases, and the automations drift apart within a month.

In this session you'll do each of those jobs with AI agents, and see where a human still makes the call. Autopilot works inside the product: in Studio it creates requirements, test cases, test sets, and expressions, and in Test Manager it evaluates requirements, generates test cases, and runs a test case autonomously. A coding agent such as Codex or Claude Code works from your terminal and does the same automation work through the uip CLI and the UiPath skills. You'll build one test case by hand first, so you can judge what the agents build for you.

Training Environment

Log in at https://cloud.uipath.com/tpenlabs using tenant AgenticTestingWorkshop. The Autopilot features in this session are on UiPath Automation Cloud, so make sure Studio, the uip CLI, and your browser all point there.

docs.title: 📄 The design document
docs.text:
Everything in this session comes from one design document for the UiBank web application: E2E UiBank Online Banking. Download E2E UiBank Online Banking.docx and save it in your workshop folder.

Download the design document (.docx)

🏦 Application

UiBank Web Application v2.0.0 (Accounts / Transfers / Loans / Profile)

🌐 Environment

https://uibank.uipath.com in Google Chrome. Fallback: https://purple-dune-0af054403.6.azurestaticapps.net

📝 What it describes

Log in, open a Checking and a Savings account, transfer funds between them, apply for a loan, retrieve it by Loan ID, and verify the user profile

The document describes the customer journey in eight steps. You won't test it as one long end-to-end run. Each step becomes a requirement and its own test cases, so a failure points straight at the feature that broke, and one broken screen doesn't hide the results of the others.

0

Login and Initial Account State

/login, /accounts

✅ Login succeeds; initial account state captured

1

Checking Account Creation

/accounts/account-apply

✅ Checking account listed in the summary

2

Savings Account Creation

/accounts/account-apply

✅ Savings account listed in the summary

3

Funds Transfer Between Accounts

/accounts/transfer-money

✅ Both balances change by exactly the transferred amount

4

Loan Application Submission

/loans/apply

✅ Loan ID generated

5

Loan Status Lookup

/loans/lookup

✅ Amount and term match what was submitted

6

User Profile Identity Verification

/userprofile

✅ Username and email match the logged-in user

7

Logout and Evidence Collection

/

✅ Session closed; screenshots attached to the report

docs.title: 🔢 The test data
docs.text:
These are the variables the design document defines. Use them in your prompts and your automations, so the requirements, the test cases, and the results all describe the same thing.

Variable What it holds Value / rule var_Username, var_Password UiBank login From the Orchestrator credential asset {YourName}_UiBankCredential. Never hard-coded. var_CheckingNickname New Checking account AutoChecking_<yyyyMMddHHmmss>, unique per run var_SavingsNickname New Savings account AutoSavings_<yyyyMMddHHmmss>, unique per run var_TransferAmount Amount to transfer 10, never more than the source balance var_LoanEmail Loan requester email The email you registered on UiBank var_LoanAmount Loan amount 5000 var_LoanTerm Loan term in years 3 (allowed: 1, 3, 5, 10) var_YearlyIncome Yearly income before taxes 60000 var_Age Requester's age 35 var_LoanID Loan ID returned by UiBank Extracted after a loan is submitted

Three things every test case must handle

  • It runs on its own. Test cases run in any order, on any robot. In the document, the transfer uses the accounts from Steps 1 and 2, and the lookup uses the Loan ID from Step 4. As test cases, the transfer opens its own two accounts and the lookup submits its own loan, at the start.
  • No accounts yet. A fresh UiBank user sees "No accounts at this time, apply for a new account today!" instead of a table. That's a valid starting state, not a failure.
  • Unknown rules. UiBank is a demo app. Balances and loan decision rules aren't documented, and data can be reset. Check the loan outcome rather than assuming approval.

docs.title: 📋 What's Test Manager?
docs.text: The planning and reporting hub of UiPath Test Cloud. Requirements say what must work. Test cases say how you'll prove it. Test sets and executions say whether it did. Requirement What the application must do, and the acceptance criteria Test case A scenario with manual steps, linked to the requirement it covers, and optionally to an automation Test set The group of test cases you execute together Execution One run, with a log, result, and evidence per test case

docs.title: 🆕 Create a new project in Test Manager
docs.text:
Requirements, test cases, test sets, and executions all live in a Test Manager project. Create yours first: everything Autopilot generates in the next parts goes into it.

  1. Go to https://cloud.uipath.com/tpenlabs, select the AgenticTestingWorkshop tenant, and open Test Manager.
  2. On the Projects page, select Create new project.

  3. In the Create new project dialog, fill in:

    • Name: {YourName}_UIB_Test
    • Prefix: {YourPrefix}, a unique code of 3 to 5 letters and numbers: your initials plus a digit, for example VC1. Everyone works in the same tenant, and each prefix can be used only once in it. You can't change it later.
    • Description: optional, for example UiBank online banking tests.

    The Create new project dialog. The screenshot uses the prefix UIB: use your own.

    What the prefix is for

    Every object in the project gets a key that starts with the prefix: with the prefix VC1, the first requirement becomes VC1:1, the next VC1:2, and so on, across requirements, test cases, and test sets. Short and recognizable beats descriptive.

  4. Select Create, then open the project. It's empty for now.

  5. Set the project's default Orchestrator folder. Test sets need it to run automated test cases later.

    1. In the project's left menu, select Project Settings, then the Automation tab.
    2. In Default Folder, select AgenticTesting.
    3. Select Save.

    Project Settings > Automation, with AgenticTesting as the default folder.

Why your name in the project name

Everyone in the session works in the same tenant. Your name keeps your project easy to find in the Projects list, and keeps your requirements, test cases, and results apart from everyone else's.

docs.title: 🛠️ Create a new test automation project in UiPath Studio Desktop
docs.text:
1. Open Studio. On the Start screen, under New Project, select Test Automation.

  2. In the New Blank Test Project dialog, fill in:

    • Name: {YourName}UiBankTests
    • Description: optional, for example Test Automation Project

  3. Select Create.

  4. Studio opens the new project. In the Project panel, expand Dependencies and check that the testing packages are there, such as UiPath.Testing.Activities and UiPath.UIAutomation.Activities.

Why a test automation project

A test automation project is built for test cases: it has the testing activities, the Given / When / Then template, and the Test Explorer panel. Each test case in it can be linked to a test case in Test Manager, and its results go back to Test Manager when it runs there.

docs.title: 🔗 Connect it to Test Manager

  2. Select Test Manager Configuration.
  3. Under Test Manager Settings, enter the Test Manager URL https://cloud.uipath.com/tpenlabs/AgenticTestingWorkshop/testmanager_, then select Connect. The status changes to Connected.
  4. In Default Project, type your prefix and select {YourName}_UIB_Test ({YourPrefix}).
  5. Select OK.

Close the project in Studio, start your coding agent in your workshop folder, and give it this prompt:

Connect the Studio project in ./{YourName}UiBankTests to Test Manager at
https://cloud.uipath.com/tpenlabs/AgenticTestingWorkshop/testmanager_ with my {YourName}_UIB_Test project
(prefix {YourPrefix}) as the default project, and show me uip rpa tm status.

Then reopen the project in Studio. The connection is stored in the project's .tmh/config.json, so Studio, Autopilot, and the CLI all use the same one.

docs.title: ⚠️ Gotchas you'll hit
docs.text:
Things every QA team learns in the first month.

🔍 Trust but verify

Autopilot and coding agents are fast and confident. Read the generated requirements, test cases, and assertions: a test that checks nothing passes every time.

🎯 Pick the right agent

Autopilot for what's in front of you in the product. A coding agent for work that spans files, projects, and products.

🧩 Independent test cases

Every test sets up its own data in Given. Run them in a different order once to prove it.

✍️ Good manual steps pay twice

One action and one expected result per step helps Autopilot generate the automation, and run the test case autonomously.

🎯 Never hand-write selectors

Capture targets from the live app into the Object Repository. A plausible-looking selector that matches nothing costs more than the capture.

🌐 One environment

Studio, the CLI, and the browser on the same tenant. Most "Autopilot can't find my project" problems are a Studio signed in somewhere else.

docs.title: ▶️ Executions
docs.text: Where every run leaves its evidence

docs.title: 🗂️ Execution types at a glance
docs.text:
Every run in Test Manager is an execution, and every execution has a type. You'll see all of them in this session:

✋ Manual

👤 A person, guided by the Manual Execution Assistant

▶️ Execute > Manually on a test case or test set

🤖 Automated

👤 A robot, running the automation linked to the test case

▶️ Execute > Automated, once the test case is automated and published

🎬 Autonomous

👤 Autopilot, following the manual steps on the application

▶️ Run autonomously on a test case's Manual Steps tab

⏳ Pending

👤 Nobody yet. Every test case gets the result None, so you can run them later, in chunks, or one by one

▶️ Execute > Pending

Local runs vs. executions

Runs from Studio's Test Explorer are for you while you build. They live in your Studio session and disappear when you close it. Executions in Test Manager are for the team: they're stored, linked to requirements, and carry their evidence. With test sets, you'll create them next.

docs.title: 🔎 Explore the Execution tab
docs.text:
Everything you ran so far left a record in Test Manager. In your project, select Execution in the left menu and explore it:

  1. The list. Find every execution so far, with its type: your autonomous run, and any manual or automated runs.
  2. An execution. Open your autonomous run. Check its result per test case, who ran it, and when.
  3. A test case log. Open the test case log. Read each step with its result, and open the screenshots attached as evidence.
  4. From a requirement. Under Requirements, open the requirement your test case covers, and find the latest result of the test cases that cover it. That's the traceability you set up with the requirements and test cases.

docs.title: ✋ Run a test case manually
docs.text:
Add a manual execution next to your autonomous one, so you can compare how a person and Autopilot record the same test.

  1. In Test Manager, open the test case you ran autonomously.
  2. Select Execute > Manually. Allow pop-ups for Test Manager if your browser asks: the Manual Execution Assistant opens in a new window.
  3. Carry out each step on UiBank yourself, and mark it Passed or Failed. Add a comment where something looks different from the expected result.
  4. If several steps in a row pass, select Set Passed Till Here instead of marking them one by one.
  5. Select Done. The new manual execution appears in the Execution tab, next to the autonomous one.

Compare the two

Open both executions side by side. Did you and Autopilot reach the same result for every step? Where you disagree, read Autopilot's screenshot for that step: it shows exactly what Autopilot saw.

docs.title: 🧭 Filter, find, and re-execute
docs.text:
1. Filter. In the Execution tab, filter the list by result, for example failed only.

  2. Find with Autopilot. Open the Autopilot panel in Test Manager and ask for executions in plain English, for example:

    Show me the executions in my {YourName}_UIB_Test project that have
failed test cases this week.

  3. Re-execute. Open an execution, select More Options or Tasks, then Execute Manually or Execute Automated. Test Manager runs the same test cases again without you setting anything up. Re-executions don't show activity coverage.

Re-executing replaces the previous results

A re-execution deletes the earlier results of that execution and replaces them, including the autonomous and manual runs you just compared. To keep them, run the test set again instead, which creates a new execution.

docs.title: ⏳ Why does my execution stay Pending?
docs.text:
An execution you started as Pending shows None for every test case by design. Nothing runs until you execute it. An automated or autonomous execution that stays Pending is different: nothing has picked it up.

Automated and autonomous runs need an unattended robot in the folder

Test Manager runs automated and autonomous executions as jobs in Orchestrator, in the project's default folder, AgenticTesting. A job starts only when an unattended robot connected to Orchestrator has access to that folder. Setups that look connected but don't pick it up:

  • Serverless. A run sent to the Default Serverless machine template, with no runtime slots, stays Pending without any error.
  • Your personal workspace robot. The robot Studio signs in with serves your personal workspace, not AgenticTesting.
  • No robot credentials. The runtime shows Connected and Available, but no robot account with stored credentials is assigned to the folder. The job stays Pending with the reason RobotNoCredentials.
  • No Windows robot, for autonomous runs. Autonomous test execution is supported on Windows only. With only a macOS robot, an autonomous run stays Pending and no Orchestrator job is created.

What to do:

  1. Tell the trainer: robots in the shared folder are set up for everyone.
  2. Once a robot is available, stop the pending execution and run it again. Orchestrator doesn't re-check a job that's already Pending, so the old one keeps waiting even after a robot becomes free.

docs.title: 💻 Stretch: read executions with your coding agent
docs.text:
Your coding agent can read the same executions through the uip CLI, and turn them into a summary or a file for a CI pipeline. In Studio's Terminal panel, start your coding agent and give it this prompt:

In my {YourName}_UIB_Test Test Manager project (prefix {YourPrefix}), summarize the
latest execution: its type, the result per test case, and which steps
failed, with links to their screenshots. Then download its JUnit XML
results into ./results. Confirm `uip login status` first.

The coding agent loads the uipath-test skill and runs commands such as uip tm executions list, uip tm executions testcaselogs list, and uip tm result download.

\"Tool 'tm' … is not discoverable\"?

The Test Manager part of the uip CLI isn't installed on your machine yet. The error message names the install command. Ask your coding agent to run it, then try the prompt again.

  3. Review what Autopilot proposes, then accept the requirements so they're saved to your Test Manager project.

Creating requirements from a document isn't among the documented Autopilot test tools in Studio yet. If Autopilot can't save them, use your coding agent.

Autopilot missing, or can't save the requirements?

Two usual causes. Studio is signed in to the wrong environment: the Autopilot features in this session are on UiPath Automation Cloud, so sign Studio in to https://cloud.uipath.com, org tpenlabs, tenant AgenticTestingWorkshop. Or the project isn't connected to your Test Manager project: check the Test Manager settings in Studio, or ask your coding agent to run uip rpa tm status in the project folder.

Read ./E2E UiBank Online Banking.docx and create one requirement per step
in section 3, Step 0 to Step 7, in order, in my {YourName}_UIB_Test
Test Manager project, with the step's acceptance criteria in the
description. Confirm `uip login status` first.

The coding agent loads the uipath-test skill. There's no import command, so it runs uip tm requirements create once per step, eight times.

In Test Manager, open Requirements and select Create for each step. Name each requirement after the step title, and copy the step's validation into the description. It's slower, but it unblocks the rest of the day.

0

Open two or three and discuss them as a group:

  • Traceability. Can you tell from each requirement which step of the document it comes from?
  • Testability. Could you write a pass/fail check for every acceptance criterion? Which ones are vague?
  • Gaps. The document doesn't say what happens if a transfer is larger than the balance, or what the loan approval rules are. Did Autopilot notice, or did it skip them? Did it invent anything the document doesn't say?

Why one requirement per step

Eight small requirements are easier to evaluate, cover, and report on than one big one. When a test fails later, you know exactly which step, and which requirement, it affects.

docs.title: 🔍 Evaluate, improve, and re-evaluate with Autopilot in Test Manager
docs.text:
Test Manager's Evaluation Agent checks a requirement for clarity, completeness, and testability.

  1. Under Requirements, open Funds Transfer Between Accounts.

  2. Select Evaluate Requirement, next to Description. Read Autopilot's findings and its suggestions.

    The funds transfer requirement, with Evaluate Requirement next to Description.

  3. Implement two or three suggestions you agree with by editing the requirement. A typical one is a rule for a transfer larger than the source balance. If the document doesn't answer a question, write it down as an open question instead of making the answer up.

  4. Evaluate the requirement again. Did the result improve? Did Autopilot raise anything new?
  5. Repeat for Loan Application Submission, the requirement with the most undocumented rules.

Add your own prompts

Autopilot evaluates requirements with the prompts in the project's Prompt Library. Besides the predefined ones, such as Multifaceted Audit, Performance Evaluation, and Security Assessment, you can add custom prompts for your team's own quality rules:

  1. In Test Manager, select Project Settings in the project's left menu, then the Prompt library tab.
  2. Select Add prompt.
  3. In Create prompt, fill in:
    • Name and Description, so others know when to use it.
    • Mode of use: Evaluate requirement quality for an evaluation prompt. Other modes include Create tests from requirement, Import test cases, and Autonomous Exploration.
    • Prompt: the instructions for Autopilot, as specific and detailed as possible.
  4. Select Create.

Your prompt then appears next to the predefined ones when you evaluate or re-evaluate a requirement.

Requirements done

Eight requirements generated by Autopilot from the design document, discussed, and at least two of them evaluated, improved, and re-evaluated.

Autopilot drafts, you decide

The Evaluation Agent is good at spotting vague wording and missing cases. It can't know your business rules. Every suggestion you accept is a decision about what UiBank must do, so a product owner should agree with it.

docs.text: Presentation + demo

docs.title: 🧩 SAP Testing
docs.text:
The same Test Cloud, applied to SAP

All day you've tested a small web app, UiBank. Now you'll see how the same Test Cloud — Test Manager, Autopilot for Testers, robots, and coding agents — tests SAP, one of the most business-critical systems a company runs. You don't need SAP experience: the key terms are below.

docs.title: 📖 SAP in two minutes
docs.text:
SAP makes ERP software: the system a company uses to run finance, sales, purchasing, HR, and manufacturing, all on shared data.

Term What it means SAP ECC / SAP S/4HANA The previous and the current generation of SAP's ERP. Many companies are migrating from ECC to S/4HANA. RISE with SAP SAP's offer for moving to SAP S/4HANA in the cloud. SAP GUI / SAP Fiori The classic Windows desktop client, and the modern web-based UI. Transaction A function you open in SAP by its code, for example VA01 to create a sales order. Transport A package of SAP changes moved from development to test to production. Each transport is a reason to retest. Order-to-Cash / Procure-to-Pay End-to-end business processes, from a customer's order to the payment, and from a purchase request to paying the supplier. Clean Core SAP's principle of keeping the standard system unmodified, with custom logic in extensions and APIs outside it. SAP Cloud ALM SAP's tool for managing implementation projects, including requirements and tests.

docs.title: 🤔 Why SAP testing is hard: the coverage illusion
docs.text:
SAP teams have long reported coverage: the percentage of transactions or test cases they ran. But coverage measures what's easy to count, not what's likely to break. Today, what breaks is often not inside SAP, but at the seams between SAP and everything around it.

🧼 Clean Core

Custom logic moves out of the ERP, into extensions, SAP BTP services, and APIs.

☁️ SaaS around SAP

Salesforce, ServiceNow, and Workday now run parts of the business that used to live in SAP.

⏩ Faster releases

SAP ships quarterly, other vendors weekly. Far more change flows through the company than ten years ago.

The typical late-release failures: integration handoffs that pass one by one but time out together, SAP Fiori screens that drift after a quarterly release, and authorization changes that quietly produce wrong results. A "100% SAP coverage" report catches none of them.

docs.title: 💼 Where customers use Test Cloud for SAP
docs.text:
🔁 Regression testing

Keep pace with SAP's quarterly updates, and run only the tests each change affects.

🚚 S/4HANA migration

Test every phase, from data preparation to cutover, and reuse the tests across migration waves.

🖥️ SAP GUI and SAP Fiori

Automate every SAP interface, with self-healing when the screens change.

🔗 Cross-system processes

Test end-to-end processes across SAP, Salesforce, Oracle, Workday, and custom apps.

What customers get: 529% ROI over 3 years with a six-month payback, 62% faster test execution, 52% less manual effort, and 55% higher test coverage. EDF Renewables automated 90% of its SAP testing in five months.

docs.title: 🚀 What Test Cloud does for SAP
🎯 Decide what to test
docs.text:
🔥 SAP Heatmap

Connects to the production SAP system and shows which transactions people actually use, so you test the business-critical ones first.

🎯 Change Impact Analysis

When a transport is staged, AI finds the processes it affects and gives you a risk-ranked list of tests to rerun, instead of rerunning everything.

🕳️ Test Gap Analysis

Finds the critical SAP processes that have no tests yet.

The usage heatmap: the bigger the tile, the more an SAP component or transaction is used.

Change Impact Analysis covers UI changes, API changes, and security changes.

docs.title: 🤖 Create and automate the tests
docs.text:
📝 Generate test cases

Autopilot creates test cases for SAP transactions from the requirements or the Heatmap data, like it did for UiBank.

🧮 Generate test data

SAP Test Data Agents create realistic data on demand, such as customers, materials, and sales orders.

🛠️ Automate low-code or coded

Business users and developers both build the automations, in Studio or with a coding agent, like you did today.

🩹 Self-healing

When an SAP screen changes, the automation repairs the selector in real time instead of failing.

Test cases generated for VA01, creating a sales order: the suggestions (left), and the manual steps of one of them (right).

Run Autonomously on an SAP Fiori test case.

docs.title: 🔗 Fit into SAP delivery
docs.text:
Test Cloud connects to SAP Cloud ALM: Cloud ALM manages the requirements, and Test Cloud automates and runs the tests across SAP and non-SAP systems, with every result linked back to its requirement. It also connects to CI/CD tools. With Maestro, one pipeline can test the whole process — the SAP transport, a Fiori approval, a Salesforce sync, and the invoice — and return one verdict.

SAP Cloud ALM orchestrates the tests; UiPath automates and runs them, and sends the results back. Confirm the integration options for each project during solution design.

docs.title: 📈 Test under load
docs.text:
Performance testing is built into Test Cloud. You reuse the UI and API automations you already have, so one set of automations covers functional and performance tests.

🧰 Dedicated load testing tools

  • A separate script set, written by a performance engineer
  • Synthetic HTTP traffic at the protocol level
VS

📈 Performance testing in Test Cloud

  • Reuses your functional automations, with Autopilot planning the scenarios
  • The real user experience through the UI, including rendering

You can run load, spike, stress, and endurance tests, in the cloud or on-premises, triggered from your CI/CD pipeline. The results appear in Test Manager, next to the functional ones.

docs.title: 📏 Measure processes, not test cases

Today you reported results per test case. In an SAP landscape, the business asks a different question: does order-to-cash work, from start to finish, across every system it touches?

🧭 Report by business process

"412 of 430 tests passed" becomes "Order-to-cash: two failures in the Salesforce handoff, both from the quarterly release."

🔺 End-to-end tests get cheap

Generated tests, self-healing, and orchestrated runs make them the baseline of every regression. Human time goes to exploring what agents won't predict.

🛡️ QA governs, agents execute

Agents generate, run, and analyze the tests. Testers decide which processes must stay green and which risks are acceptable.

  1. Go to uibank.uipath.com/register-account, or the fallback if it doesn't load.
  2. Fill in the form: first, middle, and last name, sex, email, username, and a password. Use a password you don't use anywhere else — UiBank is a public demo site.

  3. Register, then log in at uibank.uipath.com/login, or the fallback, to check the account works.

  4. If UiBank shows an Important Notice dialog after you sign in, select I agree to the Privacy Policy. Closing it with ✕ leaves you logged out. Accept it now, by hand, before you automate anything.

If uibank.uipath.com doesn't load

Use the fallback, purple-dune-0af054403.6.azurestaticapps.net. It serves the same UiBank application, with the same pages: add /register-account or /login to it. If you switch, check that your user can log in there, and register it again if it can't. The tests never store your password in the project. They read it from an Orchestrator credential asset. Create it by hand:

  2. Select Add > Credential, and name it {YourName}_UiBankCredential.
  3. Type your UiBank username and password there, then save.

Don't give the password to your coding agent

The uip CLI takes a credential only as username:password on the command line, so a coding agent asks for it in the chat. The password then ends up in the transcript and in a command. Type it in Orchestrator instead.

Write down your UiBank email

docs.title: Test Cases
docs.text: Hands-on · Part 2 of 4

docs.title: 🧪 Test Cases
docs.text: Generate them, automate one by hand, then let the agents do the rest

docs.title: 🤖 Ask Autopilot in Test Manager to create test cases
docs.text:
The Test Case Generation Agent writes test cases from a requirement, with manual steps and expected results.

  1. In Test Manager, under Requirements, open a requirement, for example Login and Initial Account State.
  2. Ask Autopilot to generate test cases for it. To steer it, pick a prompt from the Prompt Library: Valid E2E Scenario Testing for valid end-to-end scenarios, or Boundary-Value Testing for edge cases.
  3. Review the suggestions. Keep the happy path, and name it Login and Initial Account State. Keep one or two negative cases too, such as a wrong password. Discard the rest.
  4. Open Login and Initial Account State and read its manual steps. Each one needs an action and an expected result you could check on screen.

Prompt Library

The Prompt Library holds predefined prompts, such as Valid E2E Scenario Testing, End-to-End Flow Verification, Rapid Test Idea Generation, Elusive Issue Detection, and Boundary-Value Testing, plus the custom ones your team saves. A prompt that works well for one requirement usually works for the next, so save the good ones.

docs.title: ✍️ Implement the Login test case by hand
docs.text:
Before any agent automates a test for you, build one yourself. It takes longer, and that's the point: you'll know exactly what to check when an agent does it in five minutes.

Every UiPath test case has three parts: Given, When, Then. Set up what the test needs. Do the one thing under test. Check what the application shows.

Create the test case

  1. In Studio, find Login and Initial Account State among your Test Manager test cases, and create a Studio test case linked to it. Name the file T0_LoginAndInitialAccountState.xaml, the same name as in the trainer's reference package.
  2. The new test case opens with three sequences: Given, When, and Then.

Given: set up

  1. Nothing to add for this test: it needs only your registered UiBank user and your credential asset. Leave Given empty. The credential is read in When, inside the browser card that types it.

When: log in and open Accounts

  1. Open https://uibank.uipath.com/login in Chrome. If it doesn't load, use the fallback: https://purple-dune-0af054403.6.azurestaticapps.net/login.
  2. Add a Use Application/Browser activity and indicate the UiBank login page.
  3. Inside the Use Application/Browser card, before any Type Into, add a Get Credential activity. Set the asset name to {YourName}_UiBankCredential and the folder to AgenticTesting. Store the outputs in var_Username (String) and var_Password (SecureString).
  4. Add Type Into for the Enter username field with var_Username, and Type Into for the Enter password field with var_Password as secure text.
  5. Add Click on Sign In.
  6. Add Check App State on the I agree to the Privacy Policy button of UiBank's Important Notice dialog, with a short timeout. If it appears, Click it. If it doesn't, carry on.
  7. Add Check App State on the Welcome! heading above "Here is your account summary". UiBank opens Accounts right after Sign In, so this heading proves the login worked. Store the result in var_WelcomeShown (Boolean).
  8. Add Get Text on the account summary area, and store it in var_AccountSummary.

Then: verify

  1. Add Verify Expression with var_WelcomeShown.
  2. Add Verify Expression that checks var_AccountSummary either contains "No accounts at this time" or lists at least one account.
  3. On each verification, turn on the screenshot option, so the evidence is attached to the result.

Run it

  1. In Test Explorer, run the test case. Both verifications must pass.
  2. Run it a second time. It must pass again.

Keep the password inside the browser card

Workflow Analyzer rule ST-SEC-008 fails the build when a SecureString is used outside the scope that created it. If Get Credential sits in Given, or the password is passed to another workflow as an argument, uip rpa validate may still pass, but Studio's build and uip rpa build fail with "SecureString variable used outside of the creation scope". Read the credential inside the Use Application/Browser card that types it.

The Important Notice dialog

From the second sign-in on, UiBank may show an Important Notice with I agree to the Privacy Policy → and ✕. Closing it with ✕ leaves you logged out, and every later step fails. Accept it once by hand before you automate, and keep step 9 in every test that logs in.

Use the Object Repository

When you indicate a target, save it to the Object Repository. The agents you use for the next test case reuse those targets, so the login fields you capture by hand are the ones Autopilot and your coding agent build on.

Login test case done

T0_LoginAndInitialAccountState.xaml is linked to its Test Manager test case and passes twice, with a screenshot on each verification. Note how long it took. You'll compare with the next test case.

docs.title: 🪄 Generate the next test case with Autopilot or a coding agent
docs.text:
Now let an agent automate the next one. Pick a requirement after Login, for example Checking Account Creation. First generate its test cases in Test Manager the same way you did for Login, and keep the happy path as Checking Account Creation.

Use the test case name Autopilot actually generated

Autopilot in Test Manager doesn't always name test cases the same way. Yours may be called Open a Checking Account, Step 1: Open a Checking Account, or something else. Check the exact name in Test Manager under Test Cases, and use it in the prompt below wherever it says Checking Account Creation. Otherwise Studio, Autopilot, or your coding agent links the automation to the wrong test case, or doesn't find one.

Then automate it with this prompt. You can give it to Autopilot in Studio Desktop or to a coding agent. The prompt is the same, only where you type it changes:

In this test automation project, which is connected to my
{YourName}_UIB_Test Test Manager project, automate the Test Manager test
case "Checking Account Creation" as T1_CheckingAccountCreation.xaml,
linked to that test case.

Use Given / When / Then. Given logs in, reusing the login steps and Object
Repository targets from T0_LoginAndInitialAccountState.xaml. Read the
credential asset {YourName}_UiBankCredential from the AgenticTesting
folder inside the browser scope that types it, and don't pass the password
as an argument. After Sign In, click "I agree to the Privacy Policy" only
if UiBank's Important Notice appears. When applies for a Checking account
with the nickname AutoChecking_<yyyyMMddHHmmss>. Then verifies that the
confirmation page shows that nickname, and that the account is listed in
the account summary with its nickname, with a screenshot on every
verification. UiBank doesn't display the account type after creation, so
don't check it.

Capture any new UI targets from the live UiBank site into the Object
Repository. Don't write selectors by hand. Inspect the project before you
edit it, then validate and build it. Ask me before you run it.
Autopilot in Studio DesktopCoding agent (Codex, Claude Code)
  1. In Studio, with your {YourName}UiBankTests project open, open the Autopilot panel.
  2. Paste the prompt into Ask Autopilot anything and send it.
  3. Review what Autopilot proposes before you accept it: does Given log in first? Does Then check the confirmation page and the account summary show the new nickname?
  4. Accept the changes, then run the test case from Test Explorer, twice.
  1. In Studio, with your {YourName}UiBankTests project open, open the Terminal panel at the bottom of the window. It opens in your project folder.

  2. Start your coding agent there:

    claude
# or
codex

  3. Paste the prompt into the terminal and press Enter.

  4. Answer its questions, and read each command it proposes before you approve it.
  5. When it's done, run the test case from Test Explorer, twice.

The coding agent loads the uipath-rpa skill, reads the project and your Login test case first, then writes the new one. If it can't reach UiBank in the browser, it doesn't guess selectors: it names the activities it couldn't target TODO Indicate — …. Indicate those in Studio, or open UiBank in Chrome and ask it to try again.

Check, validate, and correct the generated test case

Whichever agent built it, the test case is yours to sign off. Before you move on, open it in Studio and check it against its Test Manager test case and the design document:

  • Given logs in and sets up everything the test needs, so it runs on its own.
  • When does what the manual steps describe, on the right screens and fields.
  • Then verifies every expected result, with the right values, and a screenshot on each verification.
  • It runs and passes in Test Explorer, twice.

Where something is wrong or missing, correct it: edit it yourself in Studio, use Autopilot on a single expression, or ask the agent to fix it, telling it exactly what's wrong.

Compare with the Login test case you built by hand:

  • How long did it take?
  • Is the result as readable as yours? Would you trust its Then section without reading it?
  • Did it reuse your login targets, or capture new ones?

Make changes in one place at a time

Studio, Autopilot, and your coding agent can all edit the same files. Close a file in Studio before your coding agent changes it, and tell your coding agent when you've changed something in Studio, so it re-reads the project instead of overwriting your work.

Autopilot for Developers

While you review the generated test case, use Autopilot on single expressions. In the Expression Editor, select Fix (the magic wand) on any expression with a validation error, or type an instruction into the Autopilot box at the bottom, for example "Build the nickname AutoChecking_ followed by the current time as yyyyMMddHHmmss."

docs.title: 🎬 Run Autonomously in Test Manager
docs.text:
Not every test case needs an automation before it can run. In Test Manager, Autopilot can run a test case autonomously: it reads the manual steps and carries them out on the application itself, then records a result for each step, with evidence.

Try it on one of the negative login test cases you kept when Autopilot generated them:

  1. In Test Manager, under Test Cases, open a test case that has manual steps but no automation.
  2. If a step logs in, write the password as {{credential:{YourName}_UiBankCredential}} instead of typing it into the step.
  3. Open the Manual Steps tab and select Run autonomously. Depending on the release, the button may be labeled Run with Autopilot.
  4. Enter the target URL https://uibank.uipath.com/login, or https://purple-dune-0af054403.6.azurestaticapps.net/login if you use the fallback. Run stays disabled until you do.
  5. Pick the model the trainer names.
  6. Turn on live streaming now, before you select Run, if you want to watch the test case run as it happens.
  7. Select Run.
  8. When it finishes, open the result. Every step's execution is documented with a screenshot of what Autopilot saw, next to the step's outcome.

Autonomous runs need Test Cloud and a Windows robot

Autonomous test execution is available only when Test Manager is delivered through Test Cloud, and it's supported on Windows environments only. It runs as a job on a Windows robot in the AgenticTesting folder. With only a macOS robot connected, the run stays Pending and no Orchestrator job is created. If yours stays Pending, tell the trainer, and start a new run once a Windows robot is available. See Why does my execution stay Pending?

Discuss as a group:

  • When would you run a test case autonomously instead of automating it? A one-off check of a new feature, or a test case that changes every sprint, are good candidates.
  • What makes a manual step easy for Autopilot to follow? The same thing that makes it easy for a person: one action, one expected result, the exact labels on screen.

docs.title: ➕ Implement a few more test cases
docs.text:
Pick two or three more requirements and repeat the cycle: generate the test cases in Test Manager, keep the happy path, and automate it with Autopilot in Studio Desktop or your coding agent. Suggested order, with what each test case's Given must set up so it runs on its own:

🧪 Savings Account Creation

📄 T2_SavingsAccountCreation.xaml

Given: Log in

Then: Confirmation page and account summary show the Savings nickname

🧪 Funds Transfer Between Accounts

📄 T3_FundsTransferBetweenAccounts.xaml

Given: Log in, open a Checking and a Savings account, read both balances

Then: Checking = before − var_TransferAmount; Savings = before + var_TransferAmount

🧪 Loan Application Submission

📄 T4_LoanApplicationSubmission.xaml

Given: Log in

Then: Result message captured; Loan ID returned

🧪 Loan Status Lookup

📄 T5_LoanStatusLookup.xaml

Given: Log in, submit a loan, keep var_LoanID

Then: Amount and term match

🧪 User Profile Identity Verification

📄 T6_UserProfileIdentityVerification.xaml

Given: Log in

Then: Username and email match

🧪 Logout and Evidence Collection

📄 T7_LogoutAndEvidenceCollection.xaml

Given: Log in

Then: Session closed; top menu no longer available

Don't assume the loan is approved

UiBank's loan decision rules aren't documented. The loan tests must pass whether the loan is approved or rejected, as long as a Loan ID comes back and the lookup shows the same amount and term.

A balance check fails?

Read the screenshot before you read the code. The usual causes are a balance read as text with a currency sign ($1,000.00 isn't a number until you parse it), or a balance read before the account summary refreshed. Autopilot in the Expression Editor is quick at the conversion: "Convert this text, for example "$1,000.00", to a Decimal."

Test cases done

At least four automated test cases, each linked to its Test Manager test case and passing on its own: Login built by hand, the rest built by Autopilot or your coding agent. Plus a few manual-only test cases from Autopilot, and one autonomous run.

Your automations don't build yet?

You can still do the Test Sets part. Link the trainer's DemoUiBankTests package to your test cases, one per step from T0 to T7. See Not enough automated test cases? in Test Sets.

docs.title: 📤 Publish your testing project to the tenant feed
docs.text:
Autopilot builds the test sets from the automated test cases it can find in Orchestrator, and Test Manager runs them from the published package. So publish first.

  1. In Studio, with your {YourName}UiBankTests project open, mark your test cases as publishable. Studio creates test cases as drafts, and only publishable ones go into the package. In the Project panel, right-click each test case you automated and select Set as Publishable. Its icon turns blue.
  2. Select Publish.
  3. In Publish to, select Orchestrator Tenant Process Feed.
  4. Bump the version if you published before, then select Publish.
  5. Wait for the confirmation that the package was published.

Why the tenant feed

Automated runs of test sets include only the test cases published to the Orchestrator Tenant Process Feed, in the latest package version. A package published to your personal workspace feed, or an older version, isn't picked up. Republish after every change to your test cases.

docs.title: 🪄 Ask Autopilot in Studio Desktop to create test sets
docs.text:
1. In Studio, open the Autopilot panel in your {YourName}UiBankTests project.

  2. Give Autopilot this prompt:

    In my {YourName}_UIB_Test Test Manager project, create two test sets from the
existing test cases:
- "UiBank Smoke" with Login and Initial Account State only.
- "UiBank Regression" with every test case that is automated
  in this Studio project.
Show me the test cases you'll put in each set before you create them.

  3. Check the proposal, then accept it. In Test Manager, open Test Sets and confirm both sets exist with the right test cases.

Why a smoke set?

A smoke set answers one question fast: is the application up and can I log in? Run it first. If it fails, there's no point waiting for the full regression set.

docs.title: ▶️ Run the test sets
docs.text:
Test Manager runs automated test cases on a robot in the AgenticTesting folder, from the package you published to the tenant feed.

  1. In Test Manager, open Test Sets, select UiBank Smoke, then Execute > Automated.
  2. When it passes, run UiBank Regression the same way.
Or ask your coding agent 
Set every automated test case in {YourName}UiBankTests as Publishable, then
publish the project to the tenant feed of the AgenticTestingWorkshop
tenant if the latest version isn't there yet, check that each automated
test case is linked to its
Test Manager test case in my {YourName}_UIB_Test project, then run my
"UiBank Smoke" and "UiBank Regression" test sets as
automated executions, wait for them to finish, and give me a report.
Confirm `uip login status` first, and stop if any step fails.

The coding agent loads the uipath-test skill and runs uip rpa pack, uip or packages upload, uip tm testcases link-automation, uip tm testsets run, and uip tm wait.

Not enough automated test cases?

Use the trainer's DemoUiBankTests package, already published in the AgenticTesting folder. Its tests are T0_LoginAndInitialAccountState to T7_LogoutAndEvidenceCollection, one per step. Your test case names come from Autopilot and won't match them exactly, so link them by step:

  1. In Test Manager, open each of your test cases, then its Automation section.
  2. Select Select Automation > Tenant Package Feed.
  3. Pick the DemoUiBankTests test for the same step, from T0 to T7.

Or ask your coding agent to link them by test case key, for example "Link my test case {YourPrefix}:12 to the test T3_FundsTransferBetweenAccounts in the DemoUiBankTests package." It runs uip tm testcases link-automation with --test-case-key and --test-name. Then run the test sets. See Resources.

The robot uses your credential asset

The robot reads {YourName}_UiBankCredential from the AgenticTesting folder, just like your local runs did. If the asset lives somewhere else, every test fails in Given, before it opens a browser.

What about manual-only test cases?

An automated execution skips test cases without an automation. To include them, execute the test set Manually, or run them autonomously.

docs.title: 🔎 Look into the executions of the test sets
docs.text:
1. In Test Manager, open the Execution tab and find the two executions you just started.
  2. Open UiBank Regression. Check the result of each test case.
  3. Open a failed test case log, if there is one. Read the failed assertion and its screenshot. Is it the test or UiBank?
  4. Select the results, then select Generate Insights. Autopilot builds a report with an Overview, Top Failing Tests, Common Errors, Error Patterns, and Recommendations.

Test sets done

Two test sets created by Autopilot, executed from Test Manager on a robot, with a result and evidence for every automated test case.

docs.title: 🛠️ Where it usually breaks
docs.text:
🚨 Run fails with "Please assign folder to project level"

Cause Your Test Manager project has no default folder

Fix Set the project's default folder to AgenticTesting, then run again

🚨 Autopilot finds no automated test cases for UiBank Regression

Cause The project isn't published to the tenant feed yet

Fix Publish it to the Orchestrator Tenant Process Feed, then ask Autopilot again

🚨 Some test cases have no result

Cause They aren't automated, or aren't in the latest published package

Fix Publish again to the Orchestrator Tenant Process Feed, and check each Studio test case is linked to its Test Manager test case

🚨 Every test fails in Given

Cause The robot can't read the credential asset

Fix Check the asset name and folder

🚨 A test passes alone but fails in the test set

Cause It depends on data another test left behind

Fix Make its Given set up everything it needs

🚨 Upload fails with "A testing project should contain at least one entry point" (error 2006)

Cause No test case is marked publishable

Fix In the Project panel, right-click each test case > Set as Publishable, then publish again

🚨 Upload rejected

Cause That package version already exists

Fix Bump the project version and publish again

🚨 Execution stays pending

Cause No robot is free in the folder

Fix Tell the trainer. Robots are shared.

docs.title: Agentic Testing & Coding Agents
docs.text: Intro + theoretical aspects

docs.title: 🤝 Agentic Testing & Coding Agents
docs.text: Learn what testing with UiPath Test Cloud looks like, what Agentic Testing adds, how coding agents work, and where the two meet in your test lifecycle.

docs.title: 🔬 Testing in a nutshell
docs.text:
Testing is an investigation that gives stakeholders information about the quality of the product under test. It happens at four levels:

1

Unit

Individual units of the system, to confirm each one's code behaves as expected. Created and run by developers.

2

Integration

Units combined and tested as a group, to find faults in how they interact

3

System / End-to-End

The complete, integrated system, against its end-to-end specification

4

Acceptance

The system against the business requirements, to judge whether it's ready for delivery

UiPath Test Cloud brings the most value in the middle: integration and end-to-end testing, which is exactly what the UiBank test cases in this session are. Two more ideas you'll use all day:

  • Black-box testing. Application testing checks that the software meets its requirements from the outside, through inputs and expected outputs, without access to its code. That's how every UiBank test works.
  • Test early. A defect found while testing costs far less than a hot-fix after it reaches production. Automation doesn't replace people: it takes the repetitive checks, so testers can focus on exploratory and usability testing.

docs.title: ☁️ What UiPath Test Cloud is
docs.text:
UiPath Test Cloud is UiPath's offering for application testers: a dedicated interface of Automation Cloud, focused on application testing, and available in the cloud and on-premises.

📋 Test Manager

Plan, run, manage, and analyze testing: requirements, test cases, test sets, executions, results

🛠️ Studio

Build automated test cases with a visual designer, or as code

⚙️ Orchestrator

Execute and manage test automation at scale, on robots

✨ Agentic Testing

AI agents that speed up test design and execution: Autopilot for Testers, and agents you build yourself

🧩 Agent Builder

Build those custom agents. Included with the App Tester license

docs.title: 🧱 The building blocks in Test Manager
docs.text:
📁 Project

The container for everything below

💡 Every object key starts with the project's prefix, for example VC1:1. The prefix must be unique in the tenant. Its default folder in Orchestrator is where automated and autonomous runs happen.

📋 Requirement

What the application must do, and its acceptance criteria

💡 Requirements can also come from Jira, ServiceNow, or Redmine

🧪 Test case

A scenario with manual steps, linked to the requirement it covers

💡 It can be linked to an automation in Studio, or run autonomously by Autopilot

📦 Test set

The test cases you execute together

💡 Test cases are assigned statically (picked by hand) or dynamically (by label). You can enforce an order only for statically assigned ones.

▶️ Execution

One run of a test case or test set

💡 Manual, Automated, Autonomous, or Pending, each with a log, a result, and evidence per test case. See Executions.

The links between them are what Test Manager calls traceability: from a requirement you can see which test cases cover it and how they did in their latest run.

docs.title: 🛠️ Test automation projects in Studio
docs.text:
A test automation project is the Studio project type for application testing. Only users with the App Tester Developer license create and publish them.

  • Test cases and data-driven test cases. A project holds many test cases. A data-driven test case runs once per row of test data.
  • Given / When / Then. Every test case has three parts: set up, act, and verify. Verifications go in Then.
  • Testing activities included. Verify Expression, Verify Expression With Operator, and Verify Control Attribute check the expected results, and can attach a screenshot to each result.
  • Object Repository. UI targets captured from the application, shared by every test case in the project.
  • Test Explorer. Runs and debugs test cases while you build. Its results last only for your Studio session.
  • VB or C#. Both expression languages are supported, and test cases can also be written as code.
  • Publishing. Publishing the project to the Orchestrator Tenant Process Feed creates the matching process in Orchestrator. Test Manager runs the latest published version.

docs.title: 🎫 Licenses
docs.text:
🎫 App Tester

Manual testing, test management, and running (not building) automations. Includes Agent Builder.

👩‍💻 App Tester Developer

Building automated test cases and testing automations, including agents

🤖 App Test Robot

Running automated tests unattended, on a robot

docs.title: 🔌 Where Test Cloud connects
docs.text:
• Requirements: Jira, ServiceNow, Redmine, and other ALM tools through Test Manager Connect, which keeps traceability between tests and requirements.
  • Version control: Git and TFS, through Studio.
  • CI/CD: Jenkins, Azure DevOps, and GitHub Actions, so test sets run as part of your pipeline.

docs.title: ✨ Agentic Testing in UiPath Test Cloud
docs.text:
UiPath Test Cloud covers the whole test lifecycle: you plan and design tests in Test Manager, automate them in Studio, and execute them from Test Manager, manually, automated, or both in the same test set. Agentic testing adds AI agents at each of those steps. They extend what a tester does. They don't replace the tester.

1

Plan Test Manager

Requirements, test cases with manual steps, test sets

2

Automate Studio

Test automation projects, Given / When / Then test cases, the Object Repository

3

Execute Test Manager

Run test sets manually, automated, or mixed

4

Analyze Test Manager

Results, test case logs, assertions, screenshots, reports

Autopilot is UiPath's native coding agent: see What's a coding agent?. The next two sections show which capability sets it offers, and where each set is available across UiPath products.

docs.title: 🤖 Autopilot for Testers
docs.text:
UiPath ships testing agents out of the box, built into Studio and Test Manager. These are the ones you'll use in the session:

📝 Autopilot panel Studio

Generates requirements from a document you give it, and test sets from your test cases, and saves them to the Test Manager project your Studio project is connected to

🔍 Evaluation Agent Test Manager

Checks a requirement for clarity, completeness, and testability

🧪 Test Case Generation Agent Test Manager

Generates structured test cases from a requirement's details, user documents, or a prompt, steered by the Prompt Library: Valid E2E Scenario Testing, End-to-End Flow Verification, Rapid Test Idea Generation, Elusive Issue Detection, Boundary-Value Testing, and your own saved prompts

🎬 Run Autonomously Test Manager

Runs a test case from its manual steps, without an automation. You can watch it live, and each step's execution is documented with a screenshot

🔎 Find with Autopilot Test Manager

Finds requirements, test cases, and other objects from a plain-English question

📥 Import Test Cases Test Manager

Imports manual test cases from an Excel file, with a prompt that tells Autopilot how to read it

📊 Generate Insights Test Manager

Builds a report from selected test results: overview, top failing tests, common errors, error patterns, and recommendations

🪄 Generate Test Case with Autopilot Studio

In Test Explorer, turns a manual test case into an automated one, using the project's Object Repository to find the UI elements

Autopilot in Test Manager can also draw on more connected sources, all enabled by default:

🧹 Obsolete Test Detection

Finds outdated or redundant test cases linked to a requirement

📈 Autopilot Chart

Creates bar, line, and pie charts from your data

📚 Documentation Search

Retrieves content from the UiPath documentation

🌐 Web Reader and Web Search

Summarizes public web pages, and answers questions that need current information from outside sources

🔌 Custom MCP servers

Run commands, and external automation processes and agents, through a custom MCP server integration

You can also build your own agents for the parts of your test process that are specific to your team. See Autopilot in Test Manager.

docs.title: 🪄 Autopilot in Studio Desktop
docs.text:
Autopilot in Studio Desktop, also called Autopilot for Developers, is the coding agent built into Studio. You give it a task in its chat, and it works on your project:

🏗️ Build and edit workflows

Creates XAML workflows from a plain-language description, and adds, removes, replaces, or restructures activities in existing ones

💻 Generate code

Writes C# coded workflows, coded test cases, and utility source files

⚙️ Configure activities

Sets activity properties, variables, arguments, and control flow

💬 Explain and improve

Explains or summarizes what activities and code do, and improves the workflow's structure and error handling

▶️ Run, debug, and fix

Runs, debugs, and validates workflows from the chat, analyzes files for linting errors, and applies fixes

📦 Packages and activities

Finds and installs the NuGet packages a workflow needs, and discovers the UiPath activities to use

🧪 Automate test cases

Automates manual test cases it retrieves from Test Manager, and creates and manages test cases

🔎 Search, plan, and delegate

Searches the documentation and the web for best practices, asks you to clarify when it needs to, makes a plan, and hands isolated tasks to subagents

🔌 MCP tools

Calls tools on MCP servers that are already configured and connected in Studio

See Autopilot in Studio Desktop for the full list.

For single expressions, Autopilot also works inside the Expression Editor, using the workflow's context — variables, data types, and the current expression:

🪄 Fix

📍 The magic wand at the top of the Expression Editor

Corrects an expression with a validation error

✍️ Generate or change an expression

📍 The Autopilot box at the bottom of the Expression Editor

Writes or rewrites the expression from a plain-English instruction, such as "Change the result of this expression to String"

📝 Generate from an annotation

📍 The Autopilot options next to a workflow annotation

Generates the activities the annotation describes

Prompting Autopilot

Be clear, specific, and concise. Say what output you expect and in what format, and set limits where you need them. "Summarize this." gets a vague answer. "Summarize the following text in 100 words, highlighting key findings." gets a useful one.

docs.title: 💻 What's a coding agent?
docs.text:
A coding agent is an AI assistant that reads, writes, and reasons about code — not just autocompletes it. Instead of suggesting the next line, it understands a goal described in plain English, explores the codebase, makes decisions, and generates entire working components. You stay in control: you review what it builds, ask it to adjust, and iterate until it's right.

Several coding agents are available today, each with their own strengths:

  • Autopilot — UiPath's native coding agent, built on the UiPath for Coding Agents infrastructure. Rather than a fixed pipeline, Autopilot runs on skills, tools, and commands. UiPath's official skills are included out of the box. You can also author your own skills and reference UiPath's skills inside them — use the built-in skills, your own, or a combination of both.
  • Claude Code — Anthropic's CLI-based agent, runs in your terminal, deeply integrated with the file system
  • Codex CLI — OpenAI's command-line coding agent, similar terminal-first approach
  • Cursor — an IDE built around AI, tight editor integration with inline generation and multi-file context
  • Gemini CLI — Google's terminal agent, strong on reasoning and long context
  • GitHub Copilot Agent — embedded in VS Code and JetBrains, well suited for in-editor workflows

What makes coding agents especially powerful for UiPath work is the skill layer: by loading domain-specific knowledge about UiPath activities, APIs, and project conventions, the agent can generate production-ready test automation — not generic boilerplate. That's exactly what the UiPath skills in this exercise do.

docs.title: 🧠 The Mental Model
docs.text:
Five concepts show up in every coding agent:

1

Tools

Built-in actions the agent can take: read a file, run a bash command, search the web, edit code, etc.

2

Skills

Domain knowledge bundles the agent loads when it sees a matching task. Like a playbook for one thing.

3

Commands

Manual shortcuts you type: /commit, /test, /deploy. Triggered by you, not the agent.

4

Hooks

Run automatically at lifecycle events: before an edit, after a commit, on session start. Used for guardrails.

5

Subagents

Specialised workers spawned by the main agent. Used to parallelise or isolate complex tasks.

Plugins

A plugin is a package that bundles any of these together — like a Marketplace app for your coding agent. The UiPath skills used in this exercise are plugins.

docs.title: 🔧 Tools, in practice
docs.text:
Claude Code's built-in tools are always available — no setup required:

📖 Read

Read any file in your project

✏️ Edit / Write

Modify or create files

⌨️ Bash

Execute shell commands

🔍 Glob / Grep

Search across the codebase

🌐 WebSearch / WebFetch

Look things up online

👥 Task

Spawn a subagent

Extension Tools (MCP)

MCP (Model Context Protocol) is the standard way to give your coding agent new tools without changing the agent itself.

  • GitHub MCP — read issues, open PRs
  • Atlassian MCP — Jira, Confluence
  • Slack MCP — read channels, post messages
  • Custom UiPath MCP — call Orchestrator, Maestro

docs.title: 🧩 Skills, in practice
docs.text:
A skill is a folder — sitting in .claude/skills/ (or equivalent), with a SKILL.md inside.

🔎 Discovered automatically

The agent reads each SKILL.md's description. When your prompt matches, it loads the full skill on demand.

📦 More than just text

Skills can bundle reference docs, code patterns, helper scripts, even compiled binaries the agent can run.

🔒 Scoped permissions

A skill declares which tools it's allowed to use. Bash access can be tightly controlled.

docs.title: 📄 What's in a SKILL.md file
docs.text:
Every skill is built around a single SKILL.md file. Here's what one looks like:

---
name: uipath-test
description: UiPath Test Manager — manage test projects, cases, sets, executions; generate reports...
allowed-tools: Bash, Read, Write, Glob, Grep
---

# UiPath Test Assistant

When the user asks to work with Test Manager:

1. Run `uip login status` and stop if the session isn't valid
2. Ask for the project name or key, then resolve it with `uip tm project list`
3. Use `uip tm` commands, always with `--output json`
4. If a command fails or a name matches more than one object, stop and ask

## References
- references/publish-and-link-guide.md
- references/failure-triage-guide.md
- references/test-result-report-guide.md

The file has four parts:

1

Frontmatter

Declares the skill's name, description, and which tools it's allowed to use.

2

Discovery prompt

The description field is what the agent matches against your request — this is how the skill gets loaded automatically.

3

Instructions

The body of the file: a step-by-step prompt the agent follows when the skill is active.

4

References

Paths to files in the skill folder the agent can read for deeper context — API docs, code patterns, example projects.

docs.title: 🔗 Where UiPath fits in this picture
docs.text:
UiPath ships a plugin for Claude Code. It bundles skills, hooks, and references — giving the agent domain knowledge about UiPath products out of the box.

npm -g install @uipath/cli
uip skills install

The plugin contains three things:

🧩 20+ skills

Domain knowledge for every UiPath product: uipath-test, uipath-rpa, uipath-platform, uipath-agents, uipath-maestro-flow, and more.

docs.text:
The plugin includes skills for every part of the UiPath platform. Three of them drive the labs in this exercise:

🧩 uipath-test Used today

Test Manager: projects, requirements, test cases and steps, test sets, executions, failure triage, and reports. Also links Studio automations to test cases.

Skills used in this exercise

The three skills in bold — uipath-test, uipath-rpa, and uipath-platform — are the ones a coding agent uses if you pick it to automate a test case or run test sets in the hands-on session.

docs.title: ⚖️ Where the coding agent fits
docs.text:
Autopilot works inside one product at a time, on what's in front of you. A coding agent works from your terminal, across products, through the uip CLI:

🤖 Autopilot for Testers and for Developers

  • Where you use it: Inside Studio or Test Manager
  • What it sees: The requirement, expression, or results in front of you
  • Best for: Requirements and test cases from a document, requirement quality, test case suggestions, fixing an expression, explaining results
VS

💻 Coding agent + UiPath skills

  • Where you use it: Your terminal or editor
  • What it sees: Files on your machine, your Studio project, Test Manager, and Orchestrator in one session
  • Best for: Work that spans files and products: checking coverage against a document, a suite of Given / When / Then automations, publish, link, run, and report

In the hands-on session, Autopilot leads. Autopilot in Studio Desktop writes the requirements and the test sets, and Autopilot in Test Manager evaluates the requirements, generates the test cases, and runs one autonomously. You automate the Login test case by hand, so you know what good looks like. Then you automate the next one with Autopilot in Studio Desktop or a coding agent, and compare the two.

docs.title: 👋 概述
docs.text:
一家银行的 QA 团队每个迭代都会拿到一份新的应用说明。有人把它整理成需求。有人在 Test Manager 里手动录入测试用例。另一个人在 Studio 中逐个重建，捕获每个字段和按钮。第四个人把它们分组成测试集、运行，再把结果复制到状态邮件里。这就是四次交接和数小时的点击操作，而且不到一个月，文档、需求、测试用例和自动化之间就会彼此脱节。

在本课中，你会借助 AI 智能体完成上述每一项工作，并看到哪些地方仍然需要人来做决定。Autopilot 在产品内部工作：在 Studio 中，它创建需求、测试用例、测试集和表达式；在 Test Manager 中，它评估需求、生成测试用例，并自主运行测试用例。编码智能体（例如 Codex 或 Claude Code）在你的终端中工作，通过 uip CLI 和 UiPath skills 完成同样的自动化工作。你会先手动构建一个测试用例，这样才能判断智能体为你构建的内容。

培训环境

使用租户 AgenticTestingWorkshop 登录 https://cloud.uipath.com/tpenlabs。本课中的 Autopilot 功能位于 UiPath Automation Cloud，所以请确保 Studio、uip CLI 和浏览器都指向这里。

一家银行的 QA 团队正在把回归测试套件迁移到智能体测试。 一份设计文档。借助 Autopilot 和编码智能体构建需求、测试用例、测试集和执行，由测试人员决定什么算通过。 📋 01 需求 Autopilot in Studio Desktop 根据文档编写需求，Autopilot in Test Manager 为其评分。 → 8 个已评估的需求 🧪 02 测试用例 在 Test Manager 中生成，由你、Autopilot 或编码智能体实现自动化。 → 已自动化的测试用例 🔎 03 执行 每一次运行（手动、自动或自主），连同其结果和证据。 → 一目了然的结果 📦 04 测试集 Autopilot 为你的测试用例分组。你来运行并查看结果。 → 一个已执行的测试集

docs.text:

下载设计文档 (.docx)

🏦 应用

UiBank Web Application v2.0.0（Accounts / Transfers / Loans / Profile）

🌐 环境

在 Google Chrome 中打开 https://uibank.uipath.com。备用地址：https://purple-dune-0af054403.6.azurestaticapps.net

📝 文档内容

登录，开立一个 Checking 账户和一个 Savings 账户，在两者之间转账，申请贷款，通过 Loan ID 查询贷款，并验证用户资料

文档用八个步骤描述了客户旅程。你不会把它作为一次很长的端到端运行来测试。每个步骤都会成为一个需求以及它自己的测试用例，这样一旦失败，就能直接定位到出问题的功能，而且一个页面出错也不会掩盖其他步骤的结果。

0

✅ 登录成功；已记录初始账户状态

/userprofile

/

docs.title: 🔢 测试数据
docs.text:
以下是设计文档定义的变量。在你的提示词和自动化中使用它们，让需求、测试用例和结果描述的都是同一件事。

变量 含义 值 / 规则 var_Username, var_Password UiBank 登录信息 来自 Orchestrator 凭据资产 {YourName}_UiBankCredential。绝不硬编码。 var_CheckingNickname 新的 Checking 账户 AutoChecking_<yyyyMMddHHmmss>，每次运行唯一 var_SavingsNickname 新的 Savings 账户 AutoSavings_<yyyyMMddHHmmss>，每次运行唯一 var_TransferAmount 转账金额 10，绝不超过转出账户余额 var_LoanEmail 贷款申请人邮箱 你在 UiBank 上注册的邮箱 var_LoanAmount 贷款金额 5000 var_LoanTerm 贷款期限（年） 3（允许值：1、3、5、10） var_YearlyIncome 税前年收入 60000 var_Age 申请人年龄 35 var_LoanID UiBank 返回的 Loan ID 提交贷款后提取

每个测试用例都必须处理的三件事

  • 独立运行。测试用例可能以任意顺序、在任意机器人上运行。在文档中，转账使用步骤 1 和步骤 2 创建的账户，查询使用步骤 4 生成的 Loan ID。作为测试用例，转账会在开始时自己开立两个账户，查询会在开始时自己提交一笔贷款。
  • 尚无账户。新的 UiBank 用户看到的不是表格，而是 "No accounts at this time, apply for a new account today!"。这是有效的初始状态，不是失败。
  • 未知规则。UiBank 是一个演示应用。余额和贷款审批规则没有文档说明，数据也可能被重置。请检查贷款结果，而不要假定一定会获批。

docs.title: 📋 什么是 Test Manager？
docs.text: UiPath Test Cloud 的规划与报告中心。 需求说明什么必须能正常工作。测试用例说明你将如何证明。测试集和执行说明它是否做到了。 需求 应用必须做到的事情，以及验收标准 测试用例 一个包含手动步骤的场景，关联到它所覆盖的需求，也可以关联到一个自动化 测试集 一起执行的一组测试用例 执行 一次运行，每个测试用例都有日志、结果和证据

docs.text:
一个 Test Manager 项目，以及一个与之连接的测试自动化项目 你需要准备
  • 在浏览器中打开 AgenticTestingWorkshop 租户上的 Test Manager。

docs.title: 🆕 在 Test Manager 中新建项目
docs.text:
需求、测试用例、测试集和执行都存放在一个 Test Manager 项目中。先创建你的项目：后续各部分中 Autopilot 生成的所有内容都会放进去。

  1. 打开 https://cloud.uipath.com/tpenlabs，选择 AgenticTestingWorkshop 租户，然后打开 Test Manager。
  2. 在 Projects 页面上，选择 Create new project。

  3. 在 Create new project 对话框中填写：

    • Name： {YourName}_UIB_Test
    • Prefix： {YourPrefix}，一个由 3 到 5 个字母和数字组成的唯一代码：你的姓名首字母加一个数字，例如 VC1。所有人都在同一个租户中工作，每个前缀在租户中只能使用一次。创建后无法更改。
    • Description： 可选，例如 UiBank online banking tests。

    Create new project 对话框。截图中使用的前缀是 UIB：请使用你自己的前缀。

    前缀的用途

    项目中的每个对象都会获得一个以前缀开头的键：如果前缀是 VC1，第一个需求就是 VC1:1，下一个是 VC1:2，依此类推，需求、测试用例和测试集都是如此。简短易认比描述性更重要。

  4. 选择 Create，然后打开项目。它目前是空的。

  5. 设置项目的默认 Orchestrator 文件夹。测试集稍后运行已自动化的测试用例时需要用到它。

    1. 在项目左侧菜单中，选择 Project Settings，然后选择 Automation 选项卡。
    2. 在 Default Folder 中，选择 AgenticTesting。
    3. 选择 Save。

    Project Settings > Automation，默认文件夹为 AgenticTesting。

为什么在项目名称中加入你的名字

本课所有人都在同一个租户中工作。加上你的名字，便于你在 Projects 列表中找到自己的项目，也能把你的需求、测试用例和结果与其他人的区分开。

docs.title: 🛠️ 在 UiPath Studio Desktop 中新建测试自动化项目
docs.text:
1. 打开 Studio。在 Start 界面的 New Project 下，选择 Test Automation。

  2. 在 New Blank Test Project 对话框中填写：

    • Name： {YourName}UiBankTests
    • Description： 可选，例如 Test Automation Project

  3. 选择 Create。

  4. Studio 会打开新项目。在 Project 面板中展开 Dependencies，检查测试相关的包是否存在，例如 UiPath.Testing.Activities 和 UiPath.UIAutomation.Activities。

为什么使用测试自动化项目

测试自动化项目专为测试用例而设计：它包含测试活动、Given / When / Then 模板以及 Test Explorer 面板。其中的每个测试用例都可以关联到 Test Manager 中的测试用例，在那里运行时，结果会回传到 Test Manager。

docs.title: 🔗 将其连接到 Test Manager
docs.text:
项目需要知道它的需求、测试用例和结果属于哪个 Test Manager 项目。任选一种方式：

在 Studio 中使用你的编码智能体
  1. 在 Explorer 面板中，右键单击项目名称，选择 Project Settings。
  2. 选择 Test Manager Configuration。
  3. 在 Test Manager Settings 下，输入 Test Manager URL https://cloud.uipath.com/tpenlabs/AgenticTestingWorkshop/testmanager_，然后选择 Connect。状态变为 Connected。
  4. 在 Default Project 中，输入你的前缀并选择 {YourName}_UIB_Test ({YourPrefix})。
  5. 选择 OK。

在 Studio 中关闭项目，在工作坊文件夹中启动你的编码智能体，并给它以下提示词：

Connect the Studio project in ./{YourName}UiBankTests to Test Manager at
https://cloud.uipath.com/tpenlabs/AgenticTestingWorkshop/testmanager_ with my {YourName}_UIB_Test project
(prefix {YourPrefix}) as the default project, and show me uip rpa tm status.

然后在 Studio 中重新打开项目。连接信息存储在项目的 .tmh/config.json 中，因此 Studio、Autopilot 和 CLI 使用的都是同一个连接。

workshop/
├── {YourName}UiBankTests/           ← Studio test automation project, connected to Test Manager

docs.title: 🚀 后续步骤
docs.text:
你构建了什么，以及可以带回去的内容

📋 需求

由 Autopilot in Studio Desktop 根据一份设计文档生成的八个需求，并借助 Autopilot in Test Manager 完成评估和改进

🧪 测试用例

由 Autopilot in Test Manager 生成的测试用例；手动自动化的 Login；由 Autopilot in Studio Desktop 或编码智能体自动化的更多用例；一次自主运行

🔎 执行

每次运行都记录了结果和证据，并可追溯到对应的需求

📦 测试集

由 Autopilot 创建、在机器人上执行的一个冒烟测试集和一个回归测试集

持续进行

  • 带着你的问题来。没有问题是太基础的，尤其是在刚起步的时候。
  • 遇到问题时告诉我们。一旦技能猜错、命令失败，或者某个步骤试了三次才成功，就立刻运行 uip feedback send。

docs.title: ⚠️ 你会遇到的坑
docs.text:
每个 QA 团队在第一个月都会学到的事。

🔍 信任，但要验证

Autopilot 和编码智能体速度快、信心足。请阅读生成的需求、测试用例和断言：一个什么都不检查的测试每次都会通过。

🎯 选对智能体

产品中眼前的工作交给 Autopilot。跨文件、跨项目、跨产品的工作交给编码智能体。

🧩 独立的测试用例

每个测试都在 Given 中准备自己的数据。换一种顺序运行一次，就能证明这一点。

✍️ 好的手动步骤，双重回报

每个步骤只有一个操作和一个预期结果，既有助于 Autopilot 生成自动化，也有助于它自主运行测试用例。

🎯 绝不手写选择器

从运行中的应用捕获目标元素到 Object Repository。一个看似合理却匹配不到任何内容的选择器，代价比捕获要高得多。

🌐 同一个环境

Studio、CLI 和浏览器使用同一个租户。大多数“Autopilot 找不到我的项目”的问题，都是因为 Studio 登录到了别的地方。

docs.title: 执行
docs.text: 动手实践 · 第 3 部分，共 4 部分

docs.title: ▶️ 执行
docs.text: 每次运行留下证据的地方

docs.title: 🗂️ 执行类型一览
docs.text:
Test Manager 中的每次运行都是一次执行，每次执行都有一个类型。在本课程中你会见到所有类型：

✋ 手动

👤 由人执行，在 Manual Execution Assistant 的引导下进行

▶️ 在测试用例或测试集上选择 Execute > Manually

🤖 自动化

👤 由机器人执行，运行与测试用例关联的自动化

▶️ 测试用例完成自动化并发布后，选择 Execute > Automated

🎬 自主

👤 由 Autopilot 执行，在应用上按手动步骤操作

▶️ 在测试用例的 Manual Steps 选项卡上选择 Run autonomously

⏳ Pending

👤 暂时无人执行。每个测试用例的结果都是 None，你可以稍后分批或逐个运行它们

▶️ Execute > Pending

本地运行与执行

在 Studio 的 Test Explorer 中运行，是供你在构建过程中使用的。它们只存在于你的 Studio 会话中，关闭后就会消失。Test Manager 中的执行是供团队使用的：它们会被保存，关联到需求，并带有证据。接下来你会通过测试集创建执行。

docs.title: 🔎 浏览 Execution 选项卡
docs.text:
到目前为止你运行的所有内容都在 Test Manager 中留下了记录。在你的项目中，选择左侧菜单中的 Execution 并浏览：

  1. 列表。 找到到目前为止的每一次执行及其类型：你的自主运行，以及任何手动或自动化运行。
  2. 一次执行。 打开你的自主运行。查看每个测试用例的结果、由谁运行以及运行时间。
  3. 测试用例日志。 打开测试用例日志。阅读每一步及其结果，并打开作为证据附加的截图。
  4. 从需求出发。 在 Requirements 下，打开你的测试用例所覆盖的需求，找到覆盖它的测试用例的最新结果。这就是你通过需求和测试用例建立起来的可追溯性。

docs.title: ✋ 手动运行测试用例
docs.text:
在自主执行旁边再添加一次手动执行，这样你可以比较人和 Autopilot 是如何记录同一个测试的。

  1. 在 Test Manager 中，打开你自主运行过的那个测试用例。
  2. 选择 Execute > Manually。如果浏览器询问，请允许 Test Manager 弹出窗口：Manual Execution Assistant 会在新窗口中打开。
  3. 在 UiBank 上亲自执行每一步，并标记为 Passed 或 Failed。如果某处与预期结果不同，就添加评论。
  4. 如果连续几步都通过了，选择 Set Passed Till Here，而不用逐个标记。
  5. 选择 Done。新的手动执行会出现在 Execution 选项卡中，位于自主执行旁边。

比较两者

把两次执行并排打开。你和 Autopilot 对每一步得出的结果相同吗？如果有分歧，就查看 Autopilot 在那一步的截图：它准确显示了 Autopilot 看到的内容。

docs.title: 🧭 筛选、查找和重新执行
docs.text:
1. 筛选。 在 Execution 选项卡中按结果筛选列表，例如只看失败的。

  2. 用 Autopilot 查找。 在 Test Manager 中打开 Autopilot 面板，用自然语言查询执行，例如：

    Show me the executions in my {YourName}_UIB_Test project that have
failed test cases this week.

  3. 重新执行。 打开一次执行，选择 More Options 或 Tasks，然后选择 Execute Manually 或 Execute Automated。Test Manager 会再次运行相同的测试用例，无需你做任何设置。重新执行不显示活动覆盖率。

重新执行会替换之前的结果

重新执行会删除该执行之前的结果并替换它们，包括你刚才比较过的自主运行和手动运行。如果想保留它们，请改为重新运行测试集，这会创建一次新的执行。

docs.title: ⏳ 为什么我的执行一直处于 Pending？
docs.text:
你以 Pending 方式启动的执行，按设计每个测试用例都会显示 None。在你执行它之前，什么都不会运行。而一直处于 Pending 的自动化或自主执行则不同：它没有被任何机器人接手。

自动化和自主运行需要文件夹中有无人值守机器人

Test Manager 会把自动化和自主执行作为 Orchestrator 中的作业来运行，位于项目的默认文件夹 AgenticTesting 中。只有当连接到 Orchestrator 的无人值守机器人有权访问该文件夹时，作业才会启动。以下设置看起来已连接，但不会接手作业：

  • Serverless。 发送到 Default Serverless 机器模板且没有运行时槽位的运行，会一直处于 Pending，且没有任何错误。
  • 你的个人工作区机器人。 Studio 登录时使用的机器人服务于你的个人工作区，而不是 AgenticTesting。
  • 没有机器人凭据。 运行时显示 Connected 和 Available，但没有存储了凭据的机器人账号分配到该文件夹。作业会一直处于 Pending，原因为 RobotNoCredentials。
  • 没有 Windows 机器人（针对自主运行）。 自主测试执行仅支持 Windows。如果只有 macOS 机器人，自主运行会一直处于 Pending，且不会创建 Orchestrator 作业。

怎么办：

  1. 告诉讲师：共享文件夹中的机器人是为所有人配置的。
  2. 有机器人可用后，停止处于 Pending 的执行并重新运行。Orchestrator 不会重新检查已经处于 Pending 的作业，所以即使有机器人空闲下来，旧的作业也会一直等待。

docs.title: 💻 进阶：用你的编码智能体读取执行
docs.text:
你的编码智能体可以通过 uip CLI 读取同样的执行，并把它们整理成摘要或供 CI 流水线使用的文件。在 Studio 的 Terminal 面板中启动你的编码智能体，并给它这个提示词：

In my {YourName}_UIB_Test Test Manager project (prefix {YourPrefix}), summarize the
latest execution: its type, the result per test case, and which steps
failed, with links to their screenshots. Then download its JUnit XML
results into ./results. Confirm `uip login status` first.

编码智能体会加载 uipath-test 技能，并运行 uip tm executions list、uip tm executions testcaselogs list 和 uip tm result download 等命令。

出现 \"Tool 'tm' … is not discoverable\"？

你的机器上还没有安装 uip CLI 的 Test Manager 部分。错误消息中给出了安装命令。让你的编码智能体运行它，然后再试一次提示词。

docs.text: 总结

docs.title: 🚀 后续步骤
docs.text:
你已完成本次工作坊

你从设置 uip CLI 开始，一路把设计文档变成了需求、测试用例，以及在 Test Cloud 中已执行并生成报告的测试集，整个过程中都有编码智能体与你一起完成构建工作。

docs.title: 🔁 继续测试
docs.text:
• 针对你自己的应用运行同样的三个实验：换掉设计文档，保留提示词。
  • 添加反向测试用例，例如转账金额大于余额或贷款期限无效，并把它们加入你的测试集。
  • 把更多测试用例改为数据驱动，让一个测试用例用多组值运行。
  • 用同样的 UiPath skills 试试其他编码智能体（Cursor、Codex）。

docs.title: 📋 需求
docs.text:
从设计文档到你愿意签字确认的需求 你需要准备
